problems.title: The wrong skill runs—or none runs
problems.description: Make skills discoverable and distinguish neighboring responsibilities.
problems.practices: Trigger descriptions, routing tests, discovery and indexing.

problems.title: The agent ignores or reinterprets instructions
problems.description: Write instructions that survive ambiguity, shortcuts and pressure.
problems.practices: Mandatory constraints, rationale, guardrails and anti-rationalization.

problems.title: Instructions consume too much context
problems.description: Keep entrypoints small and load detailed guidance only when needed.
problems.practices: Progressive disclosure, pruning and conditional references.

problems.title: Skills and agents have overlapping responsibilities
problems.description: Give each procedure and responsibility one clear owner.
problems.practices: Composition, bounded roles, shared procedures and adapters.

problems.title: The agent lacks required inputs or context
problems.description: Specify inputs, configuration, evidence and resource resolution.
problems.practices: Runtime values, source access, assumptions and repository context.

problems.title: Delegated work loses scope or results
problems.description: Define bounded assignments and verifiable handoff contracts.
problems.practices: Worker scope, isolation, aggregation and coordination.

problems.title: Outputs are inconsistent or unusable
problems.description: Define what the consumer receives and who owns its format.
problems.practices: Templates, schemas, placeholders and evidence-backed reports.

problems.title: The agent stops before work is complete
problems.description: Define observable completion and account for every obligation.
problems.practices: Completion criteria, verification evidence and completeness sweeps.

problems.title: The agent repeats mistakes or loses progress
problems.description: Preserve useful lessons and resume from verified state.
problems.practices: Gotchas, memory, ledgers and resume notes.

problems.title: I cannot tell whether my guidance works
problems.description: Evaluate observable behavior and improve guidance from evidence.
problems.practices: Routing fixtures, tool traces, pressure tests and controlled comparisons.

materials.title: Direct Evidence, Safety Assumptions, and Risk-Based Verification
materials.use_when: Agents can mistake a green build or a dry-run label for proof of safe behavior. Risky changes need direct evidence of the artifact and the assumption that limits harm.
provides: Prove the real artifact rather than trusting proxies or reports
Scale verification rigor to impact and reversibility
Prove the key safety assumption behind a change
Verify dry-run claims by inspecting actual network, file, and repository effects

materials.title: Live Verification Harness, Feature Maps, and Instance Lifecycle
materials.use_when: A verification procedure drifts when routes change or failed runs leave stale instances. Agents need a repository-specific harness, maintained feature paths, and evidence that survives cleanup.
provides: Create a repository-specific live verification harness
Maintain verification feature maps with source and live checks
Health-check and reset verification instances after unexpected drive failures
Clean up only owned verification processes and preserve collected proof artifacts

materials.title: Independent Patch Verification and Baseline Comparison
materials.use_when: CI can pass for a patch that nobody independently exercised. Rebases can also make an old verification verdict describe different code.
provides: Verify each PR independently at the reviewed patch before merging
Compare changed behavior with current trunk on the same user-visible path
Verify repaired behavior with focused tests, full regression checks, and runtime checks

materials.title: Functional-Slice Tests, Observable Results, and Test Boundaries
materials.use_when: Tests can confirm internal calls while the user-visible result is wrong. A change that crosses storage or service boundaries needs a focused functional slice at a real observable seam.
provides: Focused functional-slice testing
Test observable behavior with exact expected results
Test observable state with descriptive tests and minimize interaction mocks
Choose test sizes by real resource boundaries and preserve the repository test conventions

materials.title: Verification Cost, Changed Scope, and Avoiding Redundant Runs
materials.use_when: Repeated green checks waste time while slow checks in the edit loop encourage bypasses. Verification must remain complete without rerunning unchanged work for reassurance.
provides: Place verification checks according to execution cost and scope expensive checks to changed code
Do not repeat unchanged verification commands without intervening changes

materials.title: Red-Green-Refactor and Failing Regression Tests
materials.use_when: A test written after a fix may pass without detecting the original bug. Behavior changes need failing-before evidence, a minimal implementation, and preserved checks during cleanup.
provides: Run a failing regression check before fixing a bug
Use the red-green-refactor cycle for behavior-changing implementation
Reproduce a reported bug with a failing regression test before applying the fix

materials.title: Live Bug Reproduction and Verification of Existing Fixes
materials.use_when: A tracker claim can lead an agent to accept an unproven fix or create a competing patch. Existing fixes need the same live before-and-after reproduction as new fixes.
provides: Verify an existing fix against baseline and patched live behavior before authoring another
Confirm a reported defect twice through the live user interface

materials.title: Root-Cause Diagnosis, Hypothesis Elimination, and Premise Checks
materials.use_when: Repeated symptom fixes can preserve the false premise causing a failure. Diagnosis needs runtime evidence, reduced reproductions, and explicit elimination of competing causes.
provides: Question a repeatedly failed premise with an actor census
Reproduce failures and fix root causes rather than symptoms
Eliminate debugging hypotheses using runtime observations
Keep suspected causes out of the initial agent task brief
Stop further feature work on broken tests or builds until the failure is resolved
Isolate and reduce failures before root-cause fixes, using history bisect when useful

materials.title: Queryable Traces and Source Attribution
materials.use_when: Large trace files encourage visual guessing and unsupported hotspot claims. Findings need a queryable representation and a link from recorded frames to source.
provides: Convert traces to queryable data and attribute findings to source symbols

materials.title: Improvement Flywheel and Enforced Lessons
materials.use_when: Repeated failures persist when lessons are stored as reminders that never constrain execution. A durable repair must target the missing fact or the mechanism that caused the failure.
provides: Improvement flywheel (classify and fix observed failures)
Turn recurring corrections into enforced mechanisms

materials.title: Evidence-Based Retrospectives and Approved Guidance Repairs
materials.use_when: A retrospective can turn unverified impressions into organization-wide guidance. Repairs need transcript evidence, routed proposals, and approval before shared instructions change.
provides: Repair broken workflow skills in a separate PR from feature work
Limit retrospective skill changes to demonstrated use or missed triggers
Turn session retrospectives into tested agent-guidance changes
Apply retrospective changes to shared agent instructions only with approval

materials.title: Session Ledger, Open Questions, and Restartable Handoffs
materials.use_when: Long sessions lose open decisions, source-reading history, and exact verification state. A restartable handoff needs a durable task ledger and visible unresolved questions.
provides: Open-question markers
Session ledger
Summarize session progress as outcomes and human-owned decisions
Preserve incomplete plans and use the project's designated task tracker
Persist restartable session handoffs with decisions, changed files, verification, and next work

materials.title: Safe Pause, Context Recovery, and Verified Resume
materials.use_when: A resumed agent can repeat finished work or overwrite newer state. Safe interruption needs a durable checkpoint and a verified restart position.
provides: Resume from the prior execution trail rather than repeating completed work
Preserve work and a resume note when pausing an agent run
Recover prior context within the workspace and verify live state

materials.title: Constraint-First Instructions and Anti-Rationalization Rules
materials.use_when: An agent can replace a required process with a faster path that appears equivalent. Critical instructions must constrain the mechanism as well as the result.
provides: Instruction robustness
Constraint-first reasoning
Include concrete anti-rationalization rebuttals, misuse red flags, and evidence-based exit checks in skills

materials.title: Concise Instructions, Explicit Goals, and Model-Neutral Procedures
materials.use_when: Vague goals and verbose, model-specific hints make procedures hard to execute and verify. Instructions need clear intent, evidence, and short commands.
provides: Write audience-specific instructions in concise, controlled language
Describe goals, proof, and constraints without prescribing skill choreography
Write skill procedures in model-neutral capabilities instead of model-specific workarounds

materials.title: Instruction Loading and Canary Checks
materials.use_when: An instruction edit can appear successful even when the runtime never loaded the file. Scope and loading must be observed before trusting behavior.
provides: Canary rule verification
Repository instruction loading

materials.title: Skill Discovery, Trigger Indexing, and Native Routing
materials.use_when: Hardcoded skill lists and duplicated routers miss new capabilities or select the wrong procedure. Discovery must use declared triggers across the full available roster.
provides: Skill discovery and trigger descriptions
Cross-scope specialist discovery
Trigger indexing
Select the applicable skill before work and follow its gates in order
Avoid installing a second always-on skill router when the agent host already routes skills natively

materials.title: Positive and Negative Skill Routing Tests
materials.use_when: A description can match its own wording while failing real user requests. Negative tests can also pass merely because no skill matched anything.
provides: Test skill routing with realistic positive triggers and neighboring negative triggers
For negative routing tests, require the intended owner skill to outrank the wrong skill

materials.title: Progressive Disclosure, Targeted Context, and Safe Trimming
materials.use_when: Loading every reference floods context, while trimming the active task can remove essential constraints. Disclosure and compression must preserve the information needed for the current branch.
provides: Progressive disclosure of agent guidance
Load relevant implementation, tests, types, and precedent instead of entire context dumps
Trim context proactively while preserving active constraints, errors, and decisions
Keep skill entrypoints concise with trigger descriptions and load long references on demand

materials.title: Delegate Bulk Exploration to Preserve Context
materials.use_when: Bulk source scans and large outputs consume the coordinator's context before it can judge the work. Exploration needs bounded delegation and compact evidence returns.
provides: Preserve agent context by delegating bulk exploration

materials.title: Bounded Agent Roles, Single Ownership, and Composition
materials.use_when: Generic agents and overlapping skills create unclear ownership and conflicting edits. Each role needs one deliverable, bounded authority, and explicit composition.
provides: Agent design and bounded responsibility
Skill composition and single ownership
Delegation engine isolation
Keep orchestration and code-writing responsibilities with separate owners
Do not make agent personas invoke other personas or add routing-only hops

materials.title: Template Ownership of Rendering
materials.use_when: A skill that restates template layout creates two sources of rendering rules. Output structure and local conditions need one template owner.
provides: Template ownership of rendering

materials.title: Skill-Owned Code and Supporting Files
materials.use_when: Supporting code drifts when skills share copied helpers or edit generated module copies. Code ownership must match the scope of reuse.
provides: Skill-owned code

materials.title: Repository Adapters, Resource Access, and Portable Skills
materials.use_when: Repository bindings and vendor controls can leak into portable skills. Installation can also lose shared references or let equivalent command adapters drift.
provides: Repository adapter skills
Resource access skills
Keep reusable skills separate from repository-specific agent instructions during installation
Include required shared references when distributing an individual skill outside its original pack
Keep vendor runtime settings in per-agent adapters or permitted metadata, not portable skill frontmatter
Validate that equivalent host command adapters stay semantically aligned

materials.title: Agent-Agnostic Contracts and Structured CLI Handoffs
materials.use_when: An orchestrator coupled to agent internals or free-form CLI output breaks when implementations change. Handoffs need explicit invocation and data contracts.
provides: Agent-agnostic handoff contracts
CLI JSON handoff

materials.title: Scoped Parallel Workers, Bounded Implementation, and Aggregation
materials.use_when: Parallel workers can duplicate effort, collide on files, or return claims the coordinator cannot combine. Each worker needs bounded scope and an evidence contract.
provides: Decompose parallel work into scoped workers and aggregate results
Delegate implementation with bounded files and success criteria, then review the diff
Parallelize independent specialist reviews, but keep aggregation with the orchestrator
Use communicating agent teams for competing-hypothesis investigations and independent subagents for report fan-out

materials.title: Delegated Worker Permissions and Centralized External Writes
materials.use_when: A delegated worker can publish to the wrong external thread or leak credentials if analysis and external writes share authority. The coordinator must retain write capability.
provides: Keep external writes and credentials out of delegated workers

materials.title: Worker Configuration, Fresh Sessions, and Standing Orders
materials.use_when: Worker behavior drifts when models are chosen ad hoc or follow-ups omit later instructions. Fresh work needs consolidated scope and unchanged standing orders.
provides: Configure model selection per agent responsibility
Start fresh subagents with consolidated instructions unless local state requires a resume
Carry immutable standing orders into every worker spawn and resume

materials.title: Pilot Runs, Rolling Worker Windows, and Progress Monitoring
materials.use_when: Scaling before one full unit works multiplies failures. Whole-batch waits and narrative status also hide stalled workers.
provides: Pilot a full work unit before scaling a multi-agent program
Refill a rolling worker window instead of waiting for whole batches
Judge agent progress by actual side effects and replace stalled workers
Prefer event-based agent wakeups with a heartbeat fallback over unnecessary polling

materials.title: Single Coordinator for Shared PR Stack Topology
materials.use_when: Parallel PR owners can corrupt a dependent stack by rebasing or retargeting it independently. Stack topology needs one coordinator.
provides: Keep stack topology updates under one coordinator while PR owners work in parallel

materials.title: Fixed Stop Conditions and Immediate Stop Propagation
materials.use_when: An autonomous loop can lower its completion bar or continue writing after an operator stop. Finish conditions and stop propagation must remain explicit.
provides: Propagate operator stop orders to all active agents as an immediate no-writes hold
Keep autonomous iterations bound to an unchanged stop predicate

materials.title: Reversible Autonomy, Approval Gates, and Uncertain Targets
materials.use_when: Autonomy can either stall reversible work or cross an authorization boundary. Planning, risky changes, uncertain external targets, and external review need distinct gates.
provides: Proceed on reversible work without human blocking
Wait for an explicit operator go before executing an approved plan
Keep verified stacked PRs unmerged until explicitly authorized
Fail closed when an external automation's target is uncertain
Escalate irreversible or high-risk work for fresh human approval even during an approved autonomous run
Require explicit authorization for each external cross-model review invocation

materials.title: Clarify Intent, Surface Assumptions, and Challenge Scope
materials.use_when: An agent can confidently solve an unstated problem or add complexity the user never wanted. Unclear intent needs a confirmed restatement before downstream work.
provides: Reject unnecessary scope instead of reflexively agreeing
Surface assumptions and stop when requirements conflict or remain uncertain
Challenge unwarranted scope or complexity while leaving informed decisions to the user
Interview for intent one question and one explicit guess at a time
